Expressing Opinions & Public Discourse

Focus: Asking and Giving Opinions, Agreeing and Disagreeing, Public Discourse, Formal Debate. Materi ini menggunakan instruksi Bahasa Indonesia secukupnya, sementara contoh, dialog, teks, dan latihan tetap dominan Bahasa Inggris.

Essential SkillAsk, give, agree, disagree, and respond respectfully.
ContextAI, flexing, smartphone rules, digital minimalism, and island students.
Final MissionFormal class debate on school policy or digital issue.
MapelBahasa Inggris
Kelas/FaseXI / Fase F
ChapterExpressing Opinions & Public Discourse
ProjectFormal Class Debate
Chapter Opening

When Your Opinion Matters

Bayangkan situasi ini.

Suatu pagi di kelas Bahasa Inggris, guru memberi tugas menulis opinion paragraph. Beberapa siswa menggunakan AI untuk mencari ide. Ada yang hanya memakai AI untuk membantu memahami kosakata. Ada juga yang langsung menyalin jawaban dari AI tanpa membaca ulang. Di grup kelas, muncul perdebatan.

AI helps students learn faster, especially when internet access and learning resources are limited.
But if students copy everything from AI, they will not learn anything.

Lalu muncul pertanyaan besar:

Should students be allowed to use AI for school assignments?

Di chapter ini, kamu tidak hanya belajar cara mengatakan “I think...” atau “I agree.” Kamu akan belajar bagaimana menyampaikan pendapat dengan alasan, bukti, contoh, dan sikap yang santun. Kamu juga akan belajar bagaimana berbeda pendapat tanpa menyerang temanmu.

Dalam kehidupan nyata, opinion matters. Pendapat yang baik tidak hanya keras, tetapi jelas, sopan, dan didukung alasan.

Before You Learn

Why This Chapter Matters

Di sekolah, media sosial, organisasi, keluarga, bahkan di masyarakat pulau, kamu sering mendengar dan menyampaikan pendapat. Misalnya:

  • Apakah siswa boleh menggunakan HP saat jam sekolah?
  • Apakah AI membantu atau merusak proses belajar?
  • Apakah flexing di media sosial membuat remaja lebih percaya diri atau justru tertekan?
  • Apakah gaya hidup minimalis cocok untuk siswa di daerah kepulauan?
  • Apakah sekolah perlu membuat aturan digital yang lebih tegas?
  • Apakah internet cepat harus menjadi kebutuhan utama sekolah pulau?
Untuk membahas isu seperti itu, kamu perlu bahasa Inggris yang tepat. Kamu perlu bisa ask for someone’s opinion, give your opinion, agree politely, disagree respectfully, give reasons and examples, respond to other people’s ideas, build arguments, and join a discussion or debate.
Learning Map

Learning Objectives

1

ask for opinions politely in formal and informal situations

2

express personal opinions clearly using appropriate expressions

3

agree and disagree respectfully

4

support opinions with reasons, examples, and evidence

5

identify facts, opinions, reasons, evidence, assumptions, and counterarguments

6

participate in a structured discussion about teen and digital issues

7

write an opinion paragraph using clear organization

8

perform a formal class debate about a school policy or digital issue

9

use English to take part in public discourse responsibly

Kurikulum Merdeka

Connection with Kurikulum Merdeka Fase F

1. Listening and Speaking

Students listen to and respond to discussions, ask and answer open-ended questions, maintain conversations, and express ideas in various situations.

2. Reading and Viewing

Students read and analyze texts, identify main ideas, details, opinions, arguments, and implied meanings in public discourse.

3. Writing and Presenting

Students write structured opinion texts and present ideas clearly using appropriate language, organization, and supporting details.

Part 1

My Initial Understanding

Activity 1: Opinion Line

Instruksi: Bacalah pernyataan berikut. Pilih posisimu.

ScaleMeaningArti
Strongly AgreeYou fully agreeSangat setuju
AgreeYou agreeSetuju
Not SureYou are unsureBelum yakin
DisagreeYou disagreeTidak setuju

Students should be allowed to use AI for school assignments.

Flexing on social media gives more harm than good.

Schools should limit smartphone use during school hours.

Online games reduce students’ motivation to study.

Students in island areas need more digital learning support.

Social media makes teenagers compare their lives with others too much.

Reflection Questions

  1. Which statement is the easiest for you to agree with? Why?
  2. Which statement is the most difficult to answer? Why?
  3. Have you ever changed your opinion after listening to a friend?
  4. What makes an opinion strong?
  5. What makes a discussion unhealthy?
  6. How can we disagree without hurting others?
  7. Why is English useful for joining public discussion?

Vocabulary and Phrases Bank

Bagian ini berisi kosakata, frasa, dan kalimat penting. Pelajari artinya dan perhatikan contoh penggunaannya.

1. Asking for Opinions
ExpressionArti Bahasa IndonesiaExample Sentence / Arti Contoh

Artinya: Apakah kamu setuju dengan pembatasan penggunaan smartphone di sekolah?
What are your thoughts on...?Bagaimana pandanganmu tentang...?What are your thoughts on digital minimalism?
Artinya: Bagaimana pandanganmu tentang minimalisme digital?

2. Giving Opinions
ExpressionArti Bahasa IndonesiaExample Sentence / Arti Contoh
In my opinion,...Menurut pendapat saya,...In my opinion, AI can help students if they use it responsibly.
Artinya: Menurut pendapat saya, AI dapat membantu siswa jika mereka menggunakannya secara bertanggung jawab.
I think...Saya pikir...I think smartphones should be limited during class.
Artinya: Saya pikir smartphone sebaiknya dibatasi selama jam pelajaran.
I believe...Saya percaya...I believe students need digital literacy.
Artinya: Saya percaya siswa membutuhkan literasi digital.
I feel that...Saya merasa bahwa...I feel that flexing creates pressure for teenagers.
Artinya: Saya merasa bahwa flexing menciptakan tekanan bagi remaja.
Personally, I think...Secara pribadi, saya pikir...Personally, I think minimalism is useful for students.
Artinya: Secara pribadi, saya pikir minimalisme bermanfaat bagi siswa.
From my perspective,...Dari sudut pandang saya,...From my perspective, AI is a tool, not a replacement for learning.
Artinya: Dari sudut pandang saya, AI adalah alat, bukan pengganti proses belajar.
As far as I am concerned,...Sejauh yang saya pahami,...As far as I am concerned, school rules should involve students.
Artinya: Sejauh yang saya pahami, aturan sekolah sebaiknya melibatkan siswa.
I would say that...Saya akan mengatakan bahwa...I would say that digital habits affect students’ focus.
Artinya: Saya akan mengatakan bahwa kebiasaan digital memengaruhi fokus siswa.
It seems to me that...Menurut saya tampaknya...It seems to me that social media can influence self-esteem.
Artinya: Menurut saya, media sosial dapat memengaruhi harga diri.
My view is that...Pandangan saya adalah bahwa...My view is that students need guidance, not just punishment.
Artinya: Pandangan saya adalah siswa membutuhkan bimbingan, bukan hanya hukuman.

ExpressionArti Bahasa IndonesiaExample Sentence / Arti Contoh

ExpressionArti Bahasa IndonesiaExample Sentence / Arti Contoh

Part 3

Language Focus: Asking and Giving Opinions

1. What Is an Opinion?

An opinion is what someone thinks, feels, or believes about something.

Opinion = pendapat, pandangan, atau keyakinan seseorang.

I think AI can help students learn English.

In my opinion, flexing on social media is not healthy.

I believe schools should create fair phone rules.

2. Fact vs Opinion

Opinion is different from fact.

TypeMeaningExample / Arti Contoh
FactSomething that can be proven true or falseSmartphones are digital devices.
Artinya: Smartphone adalah perangkat digital.
OpinionSomeone’s belief, view, or feelingSmartphones are too distracting for students.
Artinya: Smartphone terlalu mengganggu perhatian siswa.

More Examples

SentenceFact or Opinion?Explanation
AI tools can generate text.FactIt can be proven.
AI makes students lazy.OpinionIt depends on how students use it.
Some students use social media every day.FactIt can be checked through observation or survey.
Social media is dangerous for teenagers.OpinionIt is a judgment or belief.
Online games require internet access.FactIt can be proven.
Online games are the main reason students lose motivation.OpinionIt needs evidence and discussion.

3. Opinion, Reason, Evidence, and Example

A strong opinion usually has four parts.

PartFunctionExample / Arti Contoh
OpinionYour positionI think students may use AI for learning.
Artinya: Saya pikir siswa boleh menggunakan AI untuk belajar.
ReasonWhy you think sobecause AI can explain difficult concepts.
Artinya: karena AI dapat menjelaskan konsep-konsep yang sulit.
EvidenceSupport from fact, observation, or dataMany students use AI to check grammar and vocabulary.
Artinya: Banyak siswa menggunakan AI untuk memeriksa tata bahasa dan kosakata.
ExampleReal situationFor example, a student can ask AI to explain the difference between “agree” and “disagree.”
Artinya: Misalnya, seorang siswa dapat meminta AI menjelaskan perbedaan antara “agree” dan “disagree.”
I think students may use AI for learning because AI can explain difficult concepts. Based on my observation, many students use AI to check grammar and vocabulary. For example, a student can ask AI to explain the difference between “agree” and “disagree.”

4. Strong Opinion vs Soft Opinion

Strong Opinion

Use strong opinion when you are confident.

  • I strongly believe that students should not copy answers from AI.
  • I am convinced that digital literacy is important.
  • There is no doubt that social media affects teenagers.

Soft Opinion

Use soft opinion when you want to sound polite or open to discussion.

  • I suppose AI can be helpful if students use it wisely.
  • It seems that smartphone rules should be discussed with students.
  • To some extent, online games can be entertaining.

5. How to Disagree Without Being Rude

Rude Disagreement

You are wrong. Your idea is stupid.

Polite Disagreement

I see your point, but I have a different opinion. I think the problem is not AI itself, but how students use it.

Don’t SaySay This Instead
That’s wrong.I see it differently.
Your idea is bad.I have a different opinion.
You don’t understand.Let me explain my point.
I don’t care.I respect your opinion, but I disagree.
That makes no sense.I’m not sure I agree with that.

Model Dialogue 1: Informal Discussion

Topic: Should Students Use AI for English Homework?

Tiga siswa sedang berdiskusi setelah pelajaran Bahasa Inggris. Guru meminta mereka menulis opinion paragraph. Mereka membahas apakah AI boleh digunakan untuk membantu tugas. Klik kalimat dialog untuk mendengarkan.

Rani: What do you think about using AI for English homework?

Sinta: I see your point, but I’m not sure I fully agree. Some students may just copy the answer without learning anything.

Rani: So, do you think our school should make rules about AI?

Arman: Yes, I strongly believe that schools should teach students how to use AI responsibly.

Sinta: I agree with that. Clear rules can help students avoid cheating.

Rani: In conclusion, AI is useful, but students must use it honestly.

Part 6

Model Dialogue 2: Public Discourse / Classroom Forum

Topic: Should Our School Limit Smartphone Use During School Hours?

Roles: Moderator, Student A: Pro limitation, Student B: Against strict limitation, Student C: Middle position, Audience.

Moderator: Good morning, everyone. Today, we will discuss whether our school should limit smartphone use during school hours. Let us begin with Student A. What is your opinion?

Student A: Thank you. In my opinion, the school should limit smartphone use during class because phones can distract students. Some students check social media or play games when they should focus on the lesson.

Moderator: Thank you. Student B, what are your thoughts?

Student B: I respectfully disagree with a strict limitation. Smartphones can also support learning. For example, students can use dictionaries, learning videos, and online references.

Student A: I see your point, but not all students use phones for learning. Some students use them irresponsibly.

Student C: I partly agree with both of you. From my perspective, the school should not ban smartphones completely, but there should be clear rules. Students may use phones only for learning activities and only when the teacher allows it.

Moderator: That is an interesting middle position. Can you give an example?

Student C: For example, during English class, students can use phones to open digital dictionaries or record speaking practice. However, they should not open games or social media during the lesson.

Student B: That makes sense. I agree that rules are necessary, but the rules should be fair.

Student A: I agree. The goal is not to punish students, but to help them focus.

Moderator: To sum up, most speakers agree that smartphones can be useful, but students need clear rules and self-discipline. Thank you for your participation.

Part 7

Reading Section

Pre-Reading Questions

Diskusikan secara berpasangan.

  1. Have you ever used AI to help you learn English?
  2. What is the difference between using AI for help and copying from AI?
  3. Should teachers allow students to use AI?
  4. What rules should students follow when using AI?
  5. Can AI help students in island areas? Why?

Reading Text: AI in Education: A Helpful Tool or a Shortcut?

Artificial intelligence, or AI, is becoming part of students’ daily learning. Many students use AI tools to translate words, check grammar, summarize texts, or generate ideas for writing. For some students, especially those who live in island areas with limited learning resources, AI can become a helpful learning assistant. It can explain difficult vocabulary, provide examples, and support independent learning outside the classroom.

However, AI also creates serious concerns. Some students do not use AI to learn. They use it to finish tasks quickly without thinking deeply. When students copy AI-generated answers, they may get good scores, but they lose the chance to develop their own skills. Writing, speaking, and critical thinking cannot grow if students depend too much on machines.

From one perspective, AI should not be banned completely. Banning technology does not always solve the problem. Students live in a digital world, so they need to learn how to use digital tools responsibly. Teachers can guide students to use AI for brainstorming, checking grammar, comparing ideas, or practicing pronunciation. In this way, AI becomes a learning partner.

On the other hand, schools need clear rules. Students should not submit AI-generated work as if it were their own. They should mention when they use AI, rewrite ideas in their own words, and add personal examples. Teachers can also design tasks that require local experience, personal reflection, interviews, or classroom discussion. These tasks are harder to copy because they come from real life.

In conclusion, AI in education is neither completely good nor completely bad. It depends on how students use it. If students use AI as a shortcut, it can weaken learning. If they use it as a tool, it can support learning. Therefore, schools should teach students not only how to use AI, but also how to think critically, act honestly, and communicate responsibly.

📜 Buka Listening Script

Good morning, everyone. Today, our group will discuss whether students should be allowed to use artificial intelligence for English assignments.

From my perspective, AI can help students learn English. It can suggest vocabulary, correct grammar, and give examples when students do not understand a topic.

I partly agree with that opinion. AI can be useful, but students should not copy the whole answer. If they only copy, they will not improve their own thinking and writing skills.

I strongly believe that schools need clear rules. Students may use AI as a learning assistant, but they must write their own ideas and be honest about how they use it.

That is a good point. In my opinion, responsible use is the key. AI should support learning, not replace effort. Students should ask questions, compare information, revise their writing, and explain their own arguments.

In conclusion, AI can be helpful in education if students use it responsibly. Schools should guide students, teachers should explain the rules, and students should keep academic honesty.

Pronunciation and Intonation

Dalam diskusi, bukan hanya kata-kata yang penting. Cara mengucapkan juga penting. Intonation can show politeness, confidence, and respect.

1. Rising Tone for Asking Opinions

  • What do you think about AI? ↗
  • Do you agree with the rule? ↗
  • What is your opinion on flexing? ↗

2. Falling Tone for Strong Opinions

  • I strongly believe that students need digital literacy. ↘
  • I am convinced that copying from AI is wrong. ↘

3. Softer Tone for Disagreement

  • I see your point, but I have a different opinion.
  • I respectfully disagree because the rule may not be fair.
  • I’m not sure I agree with that.

4. Pauses for Clarity

  • In my opinion, / AI can help students / if they use it responsibly.
  • I see your point, / but I believe / students still need clear rules.
Part 12

Common Mistakes

Mistake 1: “I am agree”

Incorrect: I am agree with you.

Correct: I agree with you.

“Agree” is a verb, not an adjective. Do not use “am” before “agree.”

Mistake 2: “I very agree”

Incorrect: I very agree.

Correct: I strongly agree.

Use “strongly” before “agree,” not “very.”

Mistake 3: “According to me”

Less natural: According to me, AI is useful.

More natural: In my opinion, AI is useful.

“According to” is usually used for other sources, not your own opinion. Example: According to the survey, many students use social media every day.

Mistake 4: Too Direct Disagreement

Too direct: You are wrong.

Better: I see your point, but I have a different opinion.

Respond to the idea, not the person.

Mistake 5: Opinion Without Reason

Weak: I think AI is good.

Stronger: I think AI is useful because it can help students understand difficult vocabulary and grammar.

Add a reason after your opinion.

Mistake 6: Mixing Indonesian Structure

Incorrect: I agree if students use AI.

Better: I agree that students may use AI responsibly.

Use “agree that” to introduce a full idea.

Mistake 7: No Closing

Weak: AI helps students. It can explain vocabulary.

Better: AI helps students because it can explain vocabulary. Therefore, students should use AI as a learning tool, not as a shortcut.

Finish your thought with a clear conclusion.

What Is an Opinion Paragraph?

An opinion paragraph is a paragraph that states your opinion and supports it with reasons and examples.

PartFunction
Topic sentenceStates your opinion
Reason 1Explains your first reason
Example/EvidenceGives support
Reason 2Adds another reason
Closing sentenceRestates your opinion

Model Paragraph: Should Students Use AI for English Learning?

In my opinion, students should be allowed to use AI for English learning if they use it responsibly. One reason is that AI can help students understand difficult vocabulary and grammar. For example, students can ask AI to explain the difference between “I agree” and “I am agree.” Another reason is that AI can support students who have limited access to learning resources, especially in island areas. However, students should not copy AI answers and submit them as their own work. Therefore, I believe AI should be used as a learning assistant, not as a shortcut.

Part 16

Formal Debate Project

Project Title

Formal Class Debate: Teenagers, Digital Life, and School Policy

Project Goal

By the end of this project, students will be able to express opinions, build arguments, respond to opposing views, and speak respectfully in a formal debate.

Debate Motions

  1. This house believes that students should be allowed to use AI for school assignments.
  2. This house believes that schools should limit smartphone use during school hours.
  3. This house believes that flexing on social media gives more harm than good.
  4. This house believes that online games reduce students’ motivation to study.
  5. This house believes that digital minimalism is important for teenagers.
  6. This house believes that students in island areas need more digital learning support.
  7. This house believes that social media makes teenagers less focused.
  8. This house believes that school rules should be discussed with students.
  9. This house believes that students should be allowed to use phones for English learning activities.
  10. This house believes that AI should be taught as part of digital literacy.

Debate Roles

RoleResponsibility
ModeratorOpens, controls, and closes the debate
Affirmative TeamSupports the motion
Negative TeamOpposes the motion
TimekeeperControls speaking time
AudienceListens and asks questions
JudgesAssess arguments and delivery

Debate Structure

1. Opening by Moderator

Good morning, everyone. Today’s debate motion is: “This house believes that __________.” We have two teams: the affirmative team and the negative team. Each team will present arguments, rebuttals, and closing statements.

2. Affirmative Opening Statement

We are the affirmative team, and we support the motion. We believe that __________ because __________. Our first argument is __________. Our second argument is __________.

3. Negative Opening Statement

We are the negative team, and we oppose the motion. From our perspective, __________. We disagree because __________. Our first argument is __________. Our second argument is __________.

4. Rebuttal

We understand the opposing team’s argument, but we disagree because __________.
Their point about __________ is interesting; however, __________.
We would like to challenge the idea that __________.

5. Closing Statement

In conclusion, we strongly believe that __________. We have shown that __________ and __________. Therefore, we support/oppose the motion.

OpposingWe oppose the motion because...Kami menolak mosi karena...
Giving argumentOur first argument is...Argumen pertama kami adalah...
Adding argumentMoreover,... / In addition,...Selain itu,...
Giving evidenceBased on our observation,...Berdasarkan pengamatan kami,...
RebuttingWe disagree with that point because...Kami tidak setuju dengan poin itu karena...
ClarifyingLet us clarify our position.Izinkan kami memperjelas posisi kami.
ConcludingFor these reasons, we believe that...Karena alasan-alasan ini, kami percaya bahwa...

Sample Debate Opening

Motion: This house believes that students should be allowed to use AI for school assignments.

Good morning, everyone. We are the affirmative team, and we support the motion. We believe that students should be allowed to use AI for school assignments because AI can support learning when it is used responsibly. Our first argument is that AI can help students understand difficult materials. For example, students can ask AI to explain vocabulary, grammar, or writing structure. Our second argument is that AI can help students in island areas who may have limited access to books or tutoring. Therefore, AI should not be banned, but students need clear rules.

Sample Rebuttal

We understand the negative team’s concern that AI can make students lazy. However, we believe the problem is not AI itself, but how students use it. If schools teach students AI ethics, students can use AI to learn, not to cheat.

Sample Closing

In conclusion, we strongly believe that students should be allowed to use AI for school assignments with clear rules. AI can help students understand lessons, improve English skills, and support independent learning. However, students must use it honestly. For these reasons, we support the motion.

Interactive Quiz: Multiple Choice A–E

Pilih jawaban yang paling tepat. Soal dibuat berbasis cerita agar kamu memahami konteks penggunaan bahasa. Tampilan opsi dibuat ringkas dan tidak terlalu lebar.

LOTS1. During English class, the teacher asks students to discuss whether AI should be used for homework. Dimas wants to ask his friend’s opinion politely. Which expression should Dimas use?
LOTS2. Nadia believes that smartphones can help students open dictionaries during English class. She wants to express her opinion. Which sentence is the best?
LOTS3. Rizal says, “Students should not copy answers from AI because it is dishonest.” Sari has the same opinion. What should Sari say?
LOTS4. A student says, “All online games are bad and must be banned.” You disagree because you think online games can be okay if students manage their time. Which response is the most polite?
LOTS5. Read the sentence: “AI tools can generate text based on user prompts.” What type of sentence is it?
LOTS6. Maya is very sure that schools must teach students about digital literacy. Which expression shows a strong opinion?
MOTS7. In a group discussion, Andi says: “I think students should be allowed to use AI because it can explain difficult English grammar.” Lina wants to partially agree but also remind him that students should not copy AI answers. Which response is the best?
MOTS8. Read the statement: “In my opinion, schools should limit smartphone use during class because phones can distract students from the lesson.” Which part is the reason?
MOTS9. A student says: “Flexing on social media can create pressure for teenagers.” Which sentence gives the best evidence or example?
MOTS10. During a classroom forum, a speaker says: “Smartphones should be banned at school.” You believe a total ban is too strict because phones can be useful for dictionaries and learning videos. Which response is the most suitable for a formal discussion?
MOTS11. Read the paragraph. “AI can help students learn vocabulary and grammar. However, some students may misuse it by copying answers without thinking. Therefore, schools need clear rules.” Which sentence shows a counterargument or concern?
MOTS12. Rina says: “Digital minimalism is important for teenagers.” Budi asks: “Can you give an example?” Which answer is the best?
MOTS13. Complete the sentence: “Smartphones can support learning. __________, they can also distract students if used irresponsibly.”
MOTS14. During a discussion, some students want to ban phones completely. Others want students to use phones freely. You want to take a balanced position. Which sentence best shows a middle position?
HOTS15. A student says: “AI must be banned because AI is dangerous.” Why is this argument weak?
HOTS16. In a debate, the affirmative team says: “AI helps island students because it can provide explanations when books or tutors are limited.” The negative team wants to rebut this argument. Which rebuttal is the strongest and most respectful?
HOTS17. A school in an island area has unstable internet. Some students use AI only when the connection is available. The teacher wants to make a fair rule. Which rule is the most reasonable?
HOTS18. A student posts a photo after winning an English speech competition. The caption says: “Grateful for this experience. Thank you to my teacher and friends for supporting me.” Another student posts expensive items every day with the caption: “Only rich students can understand this lifestyle.” Which opinion is the most balanced?
HOTS19. You are asked to give an opinion about online games and study motivation. Which answer is the strongest because it has opinion, reason, and example?
HOTS20. In a classroom forum, one student says: “School rules should be discussed with students because students are the people who experience the rules every day. If students are involved, they may understand the rules better and follow them more responsibly.” What makes this opinion strong?

15CThe argument is weak because it lacks explanation and evidence.
16BIt responds respectfully and gives a logical concern.
17BIt is fair, realistic, and supports responsible AI use.
18BIt distinguishes positive sharing from harmful flexing.
19CIt has opinion, reason, and example.

Part 22

Enrichment and Remedial

Enrichment Activities

  1. Write a 250-word opinion essay about AI in education.
  2. Create a digital poster about responsible social media use.
  3. Interview three friends about smartphone rules and present the results.
  4. Prepare a debate speech with evidence and examples.
  5. Compare two opinions from online articles and evaluate which one is stronger.

Remedial Activities

  1. Memorize 10 basic opinion expressions.
  2. Complete sentence frames such as “I think ___ because ___.”
  3. Practice short dialogues with a partner.
  4. Sort sentences into fact and opinion.
  5. Write one simple opinion paragraph using the writing frame.
  6. Practice polite disagreement using three expressions: I see your point, but...; I respectfully disagree because...; I’m not sure I agree with that.
Part 23

Mini Language Lab

Lab 1: Fix the Mistake

Correct the sentences, then click Check Lab 1.

Lab 2: Build a Better Opinion

Make each opinion stronger by adding a reason and example. Klik tombol untuk melihat contoh model.

1. I think AI is useful.

Model answer

I think AI is useful because it can help students understand difficult vocabulary. For example, students can ask AI to explain grammar in simpler words.

2. I believe flexing is harmful.

Model answer

I believe flexing is harmful because it can make teenagers compare themselves with others. For example, some students may feel inferior after seeing expensive items online.

3. I think phones should be limited.

Model answer

I think phones should be limited during class because they can distract students. For example, some students open games or social media instead of listening to the teacher.

4. I believe online games affect students.

Model answer

I believe online games affect students if they play too long because they may sleep late and ignore homework. For example, some students feel sleepy in class after gaming at night.

5. I think minimalism is important.

Model answer

I think minimalism is important because it helps students focus on meaningful things. For example, reducing unnecessary screen time can give students more time to study and rest.

Part 24

Chapter Summary

In this chapter, you have learned how to:

  • ask for opinions politely,
  • give opinions clearly,
  • agree and disagree respectfully,
  • support opinions with reasons and examples,
  • identify facts and opinions,
  • analyze public discourse,
  • write an opinion paragraph,
  • participate in a classroom discussion,
  • prepare and perform a formal debate.
A good opinion is not only about what you believe.
A good opinion is clear, respectful, logical, and supported by reasons.
